prompt: Rain-wet highway at night, a bootleg convoy on the move. We look in from outside a moving 1920s sedan, through its open front side window, at a Chinese American man of about 50: thin face, sunken cheeks, sharp chin, clean-shaven, round wire glasses, homburg, three-piece suit, sitting very upright and turned three-quarter toward us. A normal lens, eye level, the dark window frame edging the picture on all sides and his face a good third of its height. A chrome wing mirror low in the corner, well clear of his chin, holds two hard white headlights from the truck behind. A pale gold dash lamp lights his mouth from below left. Past him, the far window shows cobalt night smeared sideways. Thanks.

Dead-on, symmetrical, from a camera bolted to the bonnet of an open 1920s roadster at a level crossing at night, windscreen folded flat. A huge bull-necked Polish American man of about 40 fills the driver's seat, his shoulders running to both edges of the picture: wide square head, flat broken nose, one cauliflower ear, heavy stubble, flat cap, chipped teeth, mouth open. His face takes a third of the frame's height. The steering wheel sits low, below his chest. A smashed striped crossing gate lies across the bonnet at the bottom of the shot, beneath his chin line. Hard pink signal light strikes his face and mouth from the front. Behind him a black locomotive bulk, white steam and orange sparks. Thanks.

A narrow side street at night, brick walls closing both edges of the frame. Lens slightly above head height at 40mm: a short fat bald white man of 45 in the near foreground tilts his broad, double-chinned clean-shaven face up to us, snub nose, mouth wide, face a third of the frame's height, one arm flung sideways gripping his hat. Further back and smaller, a very tall thin Black man of 60 stands bolt upright on the kerb, long hollow face, both fists raised. Further still, a wiry Mexican American man of 20 crouches on a 1920s sedan's bonnet, head thrown back. That sedan burns against a lamp post in orange flame, under a blank bulb-edged theatre marquee whose teal light falls on the bald man's face. Thanks.

Head-on from the foredeck of a mahogany rum-runner's speedboat, 35mm lens at his chest height, night fog tearing past. A Black seaman of about 55 stands at the spoked wheel, the wheel low in frame below his chest: broad flat face, wide nose, heavy cheeks, grey stubble, gap in his lower teeth, navy watch cap, open neck. His mouth is wide open in song, his face filling a third of the frame and squared to us. Behind his head a hard blue searchlight from an unseen patrol boat burns a cone through the fog. Amber light from the instrument lamps lifts onto his mouth and jaw. The picture fills the frame edge to edge, with bare unmarked hull and deck. Thanks.

Long 135mm lens from the far rail of a low grey rum boat at night, the deck compressed and the sea stacked up behind him. A pale Irish American of about 30 stands three-quarter to us, his face filling a third of the frame: freckles across a narrow nose broken once, red hair under a black fedora, a boxer's split through one eyebrow, clean-shaven, chipped front tooth, shirt open at the throat. He sings mid-word, unbothered. Behind his shoulder, out of focus and huge, a column of water from a warning shot stands lit red and pink. A green running lamp beside him throws clean green light across his cheek and mouth. Wet deck to every edge of the frame, no markings on the boat. Thanks.

Camera a hand's width above black water, 24mm lens, close off the stern quarter of a small wooden skiff crossing the frame at night. A slim Filipino American deckhand of about 28 sits at the oars, three-quarter to us and leaning toward the lens: wide cheekbones, small flat nose, narrow chin, smooth clean-shaven skin, hatless, soaked black hair stuck to his forehead, wet undershirt. His face fills a third of the frame, oar handles low below his chest. Far behind him the crew's own boat burns against a timber pier, orange fire spilling across the water toward us. A cold blue-green lantern on the skiff's stern seat lights his mouth from below. The water runs unbroken to the frame's edges. Thanks.

Looking almost straight down from high in a schooner's rigging at night, 18mm lens, the masts converging to a point far below. A barrel-chested Portuguese American of about 60 clings to the ropes just under the lens, face tipped up and square to us, looking just above the camera: heavy single brow, big jug ears, bulbous nose, deep-cut jowls, white stubble, tweed cap pushed back, missing eye tooth. His face fills a third of the frame, ropes running beside it and never across it. Far beneath his shoulders, sacks of bottles swing out over the side toward two small motorboats with red lamps on violet water. A hanging yellow lamp beside the lens lights his whole face. Dark sea fills all the corners, nothing written on anything. Thanks.

Square-on and dead level with the open door of a boxcar in a wet freight yard at night, 50mm lens, the door frame set symmetrically like a stage. A very thin, elegant Black Pullman porter of about 65 sits in the doorway facing us, hatless: long narrow skull, white cropped hair, sunken cheeks, high hollow temples, long upper lip, clean-shaven, bow tie hanging undone from an open collar well below his chin. His face fills a third of the frame. Unmarked whiskey crates are stacked in the dark behind him. Through the far door, small and soft, a yard guard's lantern approaches in the steam. Magenta signal light falls full across his mouth and cheek, green signal light rims his other side, both glowing in steam and wet ballast to the frame's edges. Thanks.

Chest-height 28mm lens tilted a few degrees off level, inside a timber dock warehouse at night under sagging strings of bare bulbs, whiskey barrels stacked into the dark. Nearest the lens, face filling a third of the frame and turned three-quarter to us, an Italian American of 25 shouts: sharp jaw, thin hooked nose, slick black hair, clean-shaven, one arm straight up holding a revolver at the rafters, well clear of his face. Behind him to the right, a head taller than anyone should be, an enormous Samoan dock worker of 35 with a broad flat nose, head thrown back, lifts a Thompson one-handed. Further back at left, barely reaching the big man's elbow, a tiny old Jewish bookkeeper of 70 with thick round glasses and big ears stands on tiptoe, revolver raised in both hands. Amber bulbs overhead, cold cyan moonlight through the slats behind, unmarked barrels to every edge. Thanks.

Wide lens almost on the flooded floor of a raided speakeasy, looking up, ankle-deep spilled liquor mirroring everything. Nearest the lens, face filling nearly half the frame height, a small man of 60 with a sharp hooked nose, hollow cheeks, jutting ears and thin grey hair roars at us three-quarter on, clean-shaven, shirt open at the neck, axe high above his head. Red light from the smashed bar falls full on his mouth; teal glows from the far wall. Further back and smaller: a giant blond Swede of 30, long-boned and pale-browed, axe raised, towering at left; a bald Black man of 50 with grey stubble, axe on his shoulder, at right; deep in the room a chubby baby-faced man of 19, wading, axe up in both hands. Thanks.

From a few steps up a narrow cellar staircase, a 28mm lens looks slightly down at a crew gathered at the foot. Closest, his face a good third of the frame, a long-faced Black man of 40 with a high forehead, narrow nose and long chin, clean-shaven, white fedora pushed up, sings up at us, overcoat open, collar flat, revolver hanging low at his thigh. On the right a smashed fuse box showers white-gold sparks that light his mouth; the left sinks into deep blue. Smaller behind him: a square-headed German American of 55, cropped grey hair, duelling scars on one cheek, Thompson aimed at the floor, standing tall on the left; a wiry Greek American of 25 with heavy eyebrows, crouched at right, looking back at the sparks. Thanks.

Tight and crowded in a low cellar print shop, a 40mm lens at chest height. Front and centre, face filling almost half the frame, a stooped Jewish printer of 70 with wild white hair, deep creases, large ears, a long nose and a few worn teeth, clean-shaven, ink-black apron over a collarless shirt, sings straight at us. A green glass-shaded lamp hanging just above the lens lights his face and mouth in sickly green. Behind him a counterfeit press burns orange, curling blank sheets lifting off it. At his shoulders, further back and smaller: a skinny young Black apprentice of 18, big-eyed, sleeves rolled, beating at flames with a rag; a beefy red-faced Irish American of 45 with a broken nose, hauling on the press lever. Thanks.

A long 135mm lens at eye level picks out a dapper Cuban American of about 35 in the foreground of a night-time hold-up, his face a third of the frame height, turned three-quarter to us, singing as if ordering coffee. Thin face, long fine nose, narrow chin, small neat ears, clean-shaven, one gold tooth, cream fedora, cream suit, tie loosened and open at the throat. A warm amber headlamp lights his mouth from the side. Behind him, soft with distance, a riveted 1920s armoured truck stands with rear doors hanging open, split canvas sacks on the wet street, unreadable banknotes hanging in the air, teal neon wash over the whole city block. Nobody else near him; two far blurred figures carry sacks. Thanks.

Looking down from the landing above with a wide 24mm lens tilted off level, onto a tall gaunt Black man of about 45 on a rain-soaked iron fire escape, mid-chase, one long arm flung wide along the railing. His face fills a third of the frame, tipped up to us front-on: sharp jaw, sunken cheeks, narrow nose, small close ears, stubble, soaked homburg with water running off the brim behind his jaw, coat collar flat. The window right beside him is bursting outward, glass hanging in the air, amber room light spilling across his mouth. Magenta neon rain fills everything else, the wet iron stairs zigzagging away to a dark street far below where small torch beams search upward. Thanks.

Dead centre and symmetrical, a 50mm lens at chest height in a grand marble bank hall at midnight. A stocky Korean American of about 40 stands square to us, face a good third of the frame: wide square jaw, broad flat cheekbones, thick neck, small ears, short straight nose, clean-shaven, bowler hat dead level, dark suit with the shirt open at the neck. His right hand holds a revolver up beside his ear, muzzle at the ceiling, clear of his face. A work lamp on the floor throws hard cold white up onto his mouth and chin. Far behind him, exactly on his axis, the round vault door hangs blown open, thick smoke rolling from it, one red alarm lamp turning the smoke and marble columns deep red. Thanks.

On a tar rooftop at night, a 35mm lens held low and to his left, tilted a few degrees. A young soft-featured Italian American of about 24 sings three-quarter on, his face a third of the frame height: round cheeks, small upturned nose, full lips, a dimple in a smooth chin, wide-set eyes, stubble just starting, hat tipped too far back so his whole face shows, collar open. A Thompson is held up on his far side, muzzle to the sky. Behind him a bullet-riddled wooden water tank on iron legs sprays a dozen thin jets, which catch purple neon from the skyline. A pale yellow bulb on the stair-head to the side lights his mouth clearly. Tar glistens wet around his shoes. Thanks.

Night on the teak afterdeck of a private yacht, 1920s, seen from knee height through a wide lens. A heavy, jolly white banker of 60, clean-shaven, round red cheeks, double chin resting above an open wing collar, white dinner jacket, stands three-quarter to us with his face taking up a third of the frame, mouth open on a big happy note. Far behind him over black water a wooden motor launch burns, small, its fire doubled on the swell. A sea-green deck lantern lights his face and mouth; the fire rims his shoulder orange. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

Long telephoto, dead front-on, inside a steel mill at night. A Black foundry worker of about 40, soot across a broad forehead and cheekbones, stubbled square jaw, heavy neck, sweat-soaked collarless shirt open at the chest, fills the middle of the frame from the chest up, singing with his chin lifted and his mouth wide. Directly behind him, compressed and out of focus, a ladle pours a molten stream into the pit, blazing orange, with five small men in leather aprons silhouetted beside it. A cold steel-cyan arc lamp hits his face from the front, clean across the mouth. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

From slightly above, a 35mm lens, a cramped tailor's back room at night in the 1920s. A thin Jewish tailor of about 55, long narrow clean-shaven face, deep-set eyes, grey temples, small dark skullcap, waistcoat, a cloth tape draped round his neck and hanging down his chest, looks up three-quarter at us and sings with weary ease, hands flat on a cutting table. Well behind him and small, two men in bandanas and flat caps scoop coins from an open brass till, a revolver pointed at the floor. A mustard-yellow shaded bulb lights his face; crimson curtain cloth glows in the dark behind. No lettering on anything. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

Eye level on a 28mm lens, at a stopped 1920s assembly line of black Model T bodies receding in a long row of hard perspective behind a Polish American factory hand of about 30. Broad, flat-cheeked face, snub nose, pale stubble, flat cap pushed back, thick neck in an open grey work shirt. He stands three-quarter on, close enough that his head and shoulders take the left half of the frame, singing flatly into the lens, arms hanging. Overhead, a mercury lamp casts sickly green down the line and over his face. A caged red warning lamp on a post beyond him throws a turning red beam across the bodies. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

Locked-off, straight front-on on a 50mm lens, inside a Chinese American hand laundry on a snowy night in the 1920s. The owner, a thin man of about 65, sunken clean-shaven cheeks, close-cropped white hair, buttoned dark jacket, stands square to us, face a third of the frame height, singing quietly with a dry, bitter calm. Beside him a tall window, frosted at the edges, glows snow-blue. Behind him pale steam rises off wash coppers, lit a soft pink by one bare bulb that also lights his mouth. At the edge of frame an iron coal stove sits black and dead, door hanging open. No lettering anywhere. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

Camera on the dirt, tilted steeply up through a very wide lens, at a crash-strewn oval track at night in the 1920s. A young Black racing mechanic of about 24, lean face, high cheekbones, clean-shaven, oil smeared on one cheek, leather cap pushed back, stands over us, three-quarter, chin up and grinning through the note, his face lit lilac-white from a floodlight tower. Behind him and small, a stripped roadster hot rod burns amber on its side beside a snapped wooden rail, and one wooden wheel lies in the dirt. Dust hangs in the floodlight beams. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

Lens at the height of the tabletop, 21mm, at the head of a long polished boardroom table in a 1920s bank. An elegant Mexican American gunman of about 35, lean clean-shaven face, sharp cheekbones, oiled black hair, cream double-breasted suit, sits three-quarter on in the chairman's seat, one hand resting a Thompson upright on his far thigh with the muzzle at the ceiling, well clear of his face. He sings politely. The table runs away behind him to a far doorway full of drifting gunsmoke; small bankers in black dive under it at the far end. Gold wall lamps warm his face; red light fills the smoke. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

Lens low on wet cobbles, wide 24mm, looking up at a craggy Irish American beat cop of about 58 who bends down toward us as though to tell a secret. Long creased clean-shaven face, broken nose, big ears, grey eyebrows, dark 1920s tunic buttoned to a collar sitting below his jaw, tall domed helmet. A streetlamp at his shoulder throws sick yellow-green over his face, and the wet stones bounce it up onto his mouth and chin. At the far end of the empty street, small and off to one side, a motor paddy wagon burns scarlet on the cobbles. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

A tilted frame at eye level, 40mm, in a 1920s bookmaker's back room during a raid. A wiry Italian American bookmaker of about 45, hollow cheeks, hooded eyes, bald at the crown, blue stubble, shirtsleeves with garters, a green eyeshade pushed high on his forehead, faces us three-quarter and sings quickly, unbothered. Behind him a wall of chalk boards carries only smudged grey marks, nothing legible. Unprinted paper ticker tape loops down from the ceiling in the background, well clear of his face. Emerald light from hanging shades falls across the room; cold white from a kicked-open door at the back lights his mouth, with blurred hats moving in it. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

Dead-centre and symmetrical, low wide lens, in a basement counting room in the 1920s. A huge Black enforcer of about 35, wide clean-shaven face, thick neck, shaved head, pale cream suit straining at the shoulders, stands square in a narrow aisle singing down at us, slow and heavy, hands at his sides out of the shot. Both walls behind him are built from banded bundles of plain banknotes, stacked to the ceiling and disappearing to a vanishing point. One hanging lamp in pink hangs left of him, one in green right of him, each colouring a side of his face, meeting across the mouth. Paper bands are blank. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

Long lens at shoulder height, as if from inside a torch-lit crowd of 1920s strikers at the iron gates of a mill. A wild-eyed Greek American dockworker of about 28, heavy black brows, curly hair, big square stubbled jaw, torn work shirt, faces us three-quarter, sharp in a soft sea of flat caps, head high, singing with his teeth bared. Out of focus behind him, torches smear gold, a black 1920s sedan lies on its roof, and petrol-blue smoke rolls through. His face catches a torch from just off frame, gold on the mouth, blue in the shadow side. Nobody's arm or tool crosses his face. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

A slightly high angle, 50mm, in a 1920s radio studio with padded walls. A slick Jewish radio announcer of about 40, smooth clean-shaven face, oiled parted hair, arched eyebrows, dinner jacket, stands three-quarter on, singing with a broad professional smile. A big round carbon microphone in a sprung ring on a stand sits low at his chest, well below his chin, its metal plain. Behind him a tall studio window is smashed, a jagged star of broken glass and a torn blind, with icy white streetlight pouring through. A ruby bulb over the door warms the side of his face, and a soft white lamp lights his mouth. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

Footlight level, 35mm, looking straight along a vaudeville stage at a Black stage magician of about 50 in black tails and a white tie. Long dignified clean-shaven face, greying hair, one raised eyebrow, standing front-on with his arms spread wide and low, singing with a showman's pleasure, his face a third of the frame. A hard pink-white spotlight from the balcony pins him in place. Behind him the crimson velvet curtains are on fire from the hem up, small flames climbing on both sides, sparks rising into the dark flies. No signs or lettering anywhere. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

Low across a card table, 85mm, felt in the near foreground as a teal blur. A silver-haired German American card sharp of about 65, square clean-shaven jaw, duelling scar on one cheek, pale eyes, black waistcoat, faces us three-quarter, unhurried and amused. His far hand is raised out to the side at shoulder height, open, palm up and empty, well away from his mouth. A low copper-shaded lamp lights his face from beneath the shade. Behind him in the soft dark, tables are tipped over, chips and cards scatter and blurred policemen in dark hats push through teal-tinged smoke. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

Camera backing away in front of him at chest height, 28mm, down a steel vault corridor in the 1920s. A sweating stocky Puerto Rican man of about 38, round face, thick eyebrows, stubble, wet black hair, shirt open under dark braces, leans into a wooden wheelbarrow low in the frame, heaped with plain gold bars, his face a third of the frame height, front-on, singing between breaths. Behind him the corridor runs to a round open vault door. Red alarm light pulses on riveted walls from behind. Cold steel-blue caged bulbs overhead light his face, and the gold bounces warmth up under his chin. The gold is unmarked. The picture runs edge to edge. Thanks.

Three-quarter from among the plants on a 65mm lens, inside a glass greenhouse at night in the 1920s. An old Colombian gentleman of about 70, clean-shaven, deep lines, heavy eyelids, swept white hair, white linen planter's suit, sits still in a cane chair with his face a third of the frame height, singing softly as if to the room. Violet light comes through the panes from outside. An amber oil lamp on a small iron table at his side lights his mouth. Dark palm leaves soften the far edge of the frame, nowhere near his face. One moth circles the lamp. Quiet, empty, nothing else happening. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

A high three-quarter angle, 35mm, looking down into a derelict warehouse where snow has drifted through a broken skylight. A bald Russian American counterfeiter of about 60, broad skull, flat nose, pale clean-shaven cheeks, heavy overcoat with a fur collar lying flat on the shoulders below his chin, looks up at us and sings with satisfaction. Behind him stands a huge black iron flatbed press, blank paper stacked in its bed, snow on its frame. Hard blue daylight lamp from one side, an orange brazier from the other, the two colours meeting on his mouth. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

From lower down the steps on a 100mm lens, the night street gone to soft blue behind, a young Black preacher of about 30, plain dark suit and white shirt with a narrow tie, clean-shaven oval face, wide-set eyes, close-cropped hair. He stands on the stone steps of a soup kitchen, front-on, hands open low at his sides, singing plainly with no showmanship. A warm lamp over the door lights his face and mouth from above and in front. Out of focus behind him along the wall, a long breadline of men in coats and flat caps stands in cold blue dark, breath showing. Full frame, no bars. Thanks.

A brick alley at night seen square-on from waist height, one amber lamp on a bracket, the shadows bottle green. A yellow 1920s sedan stands nose to the right on wet cobbles. One man leans from its window: his whole head in a hand-knitted cream wool balaclava with no eye holes and no mouth hole, one thin black ring stitched around the face, and high inside it, over where one eye would be, pushed up near the ring's edge and well off centre, one small solid red felt triangle with rounded corners. Collar up, gloved. A tight chain runs from the bumper to one small green safe, half out of a broken hole in the wall. The rest of the alley is empty. Thanks.

Low wide view from just above the concrete, right beside the front wheel of a stripped teal 1920s hot rod: no fenders, no bonnet, bare engine, one goggled driver hunched behind a cut-down screen. The car fills the left half of the frame, sharp. Half a length behind on the right, one black hot rod of the same kind, its driver low. They run on the dry floor of a sloped concrete river channel at dusk, with a heavy arched bridge just ahead throwing its shadow. Burnt orange sky above the channel walls, teal gloom in the arch. No water, no other vehicles. Thanks.

Extreme close view from kerb height, the lens a foot from the front wheel and running board of a dark 1920s car, which fill the whole frame: wooden spokes, a tall narrow tyre, a sweeping mudguard beaded with water, the ribbed running board cutting across the top. Hard red light rakes along the tyre from behind, and everything in shadow falls to cobalt blue. Below, wet cobbles shine in a thin strip. The car itself is crisp and heavy, with no people, no background to speak of, and no lettering anywhere. Thanks.

A wide lens almost touching a wet night road, looking along it. The surface takes up the bottom two-thirds of the frame, black and streaming, with long reflections of hot pink and cyan neon running toward us. Ahead on the crown of the road, small and dead centre, the square tail of one 1920s car: spare wheel on the back, one small red tail lamp, spray lifting off its rear tyres. Dark shopfronts close in on both sides, their signs only coloured glows with no letters. The street is otherwise empty. Thanks.

Medium close-up, shot from outside a 1920s car through its flat side window, with a normal lens and water beading on the glass. The driver sits in profile turning three-quarters to us: a man of about 30 with a narrow, sharp face, hollow cheeks, a thin bent nose, heavy low brows, flat cap, dark coat. His mouth is shut. Gloved hands grip the top of the big wheel. A slanting band of acid green light crosses his cheek and a band of violet crosses his chest, the rest of the cabin black. Behind him, through the far window, only dark. Thanks.

A static camera at kerb height on a rain-soaked night street, a cast-iron lamp post close beside the lens taking up the left edge of the frame, its gaslight a cold green. Coming straight at us down the near lane, slightly right of centre, one open 1920s roadster with two round headlamps blazing, one driver behind the screen, a rooster tail of spray lit orange by a distant warehouse fire behind it. Wet cobbles, shuttered brick buildings, an otherwise empty street. Nothing carries lettering. Thanks.

A long telephoto view from across a wide night avenue, the perspective flattened. A cream 1920s roadster with its top down sits sharp in the middle of the frame in clean side profile, whitewall tyres, one driver in a dark hat low at the wheel. Directly behind it, packed and compressed, a wall of lit storefronts glowing purple and gold, shop windows and awnings with no readable signs. A thin ribbon of wet road along the bottom catches both colours. No pedestrians, no other vehicles. The car is crisp from bumper to bumper. Thanks.

Ground-level shot on a dark street at night, a very low wide lens looking up the road. Thick tyre smoke rolls in from the left, backlit magenta by a glow somewhere behind it, filling most of the frame. One round 1920s headlamp burns through the smoke, a hard white-yellow disc with a soft halo, with just the edge of a mudguard and one tall front tyre dark beneath it. The car sits crouched, nose toward us, its other side lost to the smoke. Black wet tarmac in the foreground, nothing else on the street. Thanks.

A very low wide angle from the marble floor of a bank lobby, looking up at one man standing over the lens, the ornate coffered ceiling arching far above him. He fires a Thompson with a drum magazine straight up with both gloved hands. An orange muzzle flash lights one side of his head: all of it in a hand-knitted cream wool balaclava with no eye holes and no mouth hole, one thin black ring stitched around the face, and high inside it, over where one eye would be, near the ring's edge and well off centre, one small solid red felt triangle with rounded corners. Collar up. Teal shadow on green-veined marble columns behind. Plaster dust hangs in the air. Thanks.

Eye-level medium shot on a normal lens, from the bank steps at night, tall open brass doors filling the background, polished and burning with reflections. A round alarm lamp above them flashes hard red with white sparking at its core. Two men run toward us, one a stride ahead, each hauling a heavy canvas sack with no markings in a gloved hand. One is big and barrel-chested, the other thin and long-legged. Long dark coats, collars up. Each whole head is in a hand-knitted cream wool balaclava with no eye holes and no mouth hole, a thin black ring stitched around the face, and high inside it, over one eye's place, near the ring's edge, one small solid red felt triangle with rounded corners. Thanks.

Inside an open 1920s touring car at night, looking from the front seat back over the rear bench with a wide lens. One man kneels up on the back seat in a dark coat, collar up, gloves on, gripping a split canvas sack against his chest, and banknotes stream from it over the folded hood into the dark behind the car. His whole head is in a hand-knitted cream wool balaclava with no eye holes and no mouth hole, a thin black ring stitched around the face, and high inside, over where one eye would be, near the ring's edge, one small solid red felt triangle with rounded corners. Turquoise light on him from one side, rose from a tail lamp below. Beyond: empty coloured dark. Thanks.

A close side view from a car's running board at night, with a slightly wide lens, one police motorcycle running right alongside and large in the frame. Its rider sits upright and heavy-set in a 1920s peaked cap, round goggles, leather gauntlets and a long-skirted tunic with a thick moustache, looking dead ahead with both hands on the bars. A red lamp on the front fork flares hard, spilling red over the tank and his sleeve. The dark edge of the car door cuts along the bottom of the frame. Electric blue dusk fills the street behind, with bare lamp points. No badges or lettering. Thanks.

The lens sits on the cobbles right beside one small green steel safe, its dented corner close enough to fill a third of the frame. A taut chain runs from its handle out of the top right corner. A wide fan of orange sparks sprays out behind where its base scrapes the stone. The street around it is cold blue-violet at night, wet cobbles falling away into darkness, closed shop fronts only as dark masses. No car in view, no people, no boxes or other objects anywhere on the road. Thanks.

A tight three-quarter close-up from just above the bed of a heavy 1920s flatbed printing press in a low brick cellar, shot on a short macro-like lens. Steel rollers and black ink plates fill the foreground. A sheet of banknotes, printed with fine dark green engraving and no legible figures or words, lifts off the bed in mid-air, more stacked behind. The far end of the machine is on fire: orange flames licking at the frame, reflected long and rippling in the polished steel. Deep indigo shadow in the cellar. Nobody in the shot. Thanks.

First-person view from the driver's seat of a 1920s roadster at night, a wide lens at eye height. Two leather-gloved hands grip a big thin-rimmed wooden steering wheel, wrenched over to the left, cuffs of a dark coat visible. A long louvred bonnet stretches ahead, a small round radiator cap at its far end, wet with rain. Past that, a narrow wet city street with coral and emerald neon on both sides pouring its reflections down the road toward us, the glows shapeless with no letters. Glass screen edge at the top of the frame. The road ahead is empty. Thanks.

Long telephoto shot at night from the far verge of a level road, flattened and side-on. Two black 1920s sedans run side by side, door to door, the nearer one hiding the lower half of the other, with one driver in each behind dark glass. A short spray of white-gold sparks bursts from where their doors touch. Behind them a low stone wall, then a dark river that stays well beyond the road, its far bank a line of amber lights against indigo sky. No lettering, nothing else on the road. Thanks.
